0edaa82bc6.q: Why did Pat McCrory implement a light rail system in Charlotte's South End instead of connecting to the airport?
0edaa82bc6.a: McCrory chose the South End because the numbers showed it could work best there. He had done extensive homework and determined that most people going to the airport do not come to downtown Charlotte, and the density was insufficient at the airport. He spent considerable time in Washington D.C. researching transportation solutions before making this decision.

3a6adbb32c.q: How did Pat McCrory reduce Charlotte's murder rate during his tenure as mayor?
3a6adbb32c.a: McCrory instituted a tolerate no truancy program, a teen curfew, and targeted the top 100 criminals in the city. He hired many police officers, put pressure on the governor and local district attorney to prosecute repeat offenders, and was very tough on crime overall. He brought the murder rate down from approximately 125-130 murders per year to 35 people per year.

7781d7aede.q: What was the Committee of 100 transportation report that influenced Pat McCrory's vision for Charlotte?
7781d7aede.a: McCrory found a notebook behind the credence in the mayor's office containing a general outline of a Committee of 100 report on transportation, including mass transit for the future. This report sparked his thinking about Charlotte's transportation needs and ultimately led to his decision to pursue a light rail project as an alternative to highway expansion.

McCrory won his 1989 city council election at-large by 300 votes over Dick Prim.

e7b2a62d4e.q: Why did Andrew Dunn write an independent biography of Pat McCrory instead of an authorized memoir?
e7b2a62d4e.a: Andrew Dunn approached McCrory unsolicited after mentioning in his newsletter that while other governors had books written about them, Pat McCrory did not. Dunn wanted to write an independent examination of McCrory's political career, not a puff piece. McCrory agreed because he wanted his record to be examined fairly with someone doing their homework, and the book covers the good, the bad, and the ugly of his political career.
